findings.finding: Nordea's Q3 2026 net fair value result fell 30% q/q (19% y/y) to EUR 198m on 'extraordinary interest rate volatility late in the quarter', while DNB's consensus has net gains excluding the pre-released AT1/basis-swap items flat q/q (793 + 383 = ~1,176 vs Q2's 958 + 194 = ~1,152), so DNB Carnegie customer/trading revenue and other MtM lines are at risk of a few hundred million NOK miss (about 2-3% of PBT).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DNB's MtM lines swing by hundreds of millions per quarter (Q1'26 other MtM +409, Q2'26 -15; trading revenues Q1 336 vs Q2 48) and are usually treated as low quality, so on their own they move the stock little.
findings.why_not_priced: DNB's consensus was collected by 7 Oct and dated 13 Oct, before Nordea's 15 Oct report, and its net-gains line ex pre-released items is flat q/q. If the read-across were priced, the consensus would show a lower net-gains number or DNB would have moved with Nordea on 15 Oct. It did not: 308.4 to 305.0 (-1.1%) against Nordea's -8.2%, and Nordea's fall was mostly its buyback pause.
findings.independence: DNB's own pre-close (2026-09-24) says DNB Carnegie FICC customer revenues are 'seasonally lower' in Q3 and 'impacted by market volatility': https://ir.dnb.no/sites/default/files/2026-09/DNB-Q3-2026-pre-close-call-transcript.pdf. Same direction, but that is guidance and not a number.

findings.finding: NII tailwinds are company-guided and modelled: the May hike's +25bp customer repricing took effect 12 July after a NOK -511m spread drag in Q2, plus about NOK +120m from one more interest day; consensus has NII +3.0% q/q (15,587 vs 15,132, range 15,444-15,756). The 24 Sept hike reprices existing mortgages and deposits only from 29 Nov, so the release's NII outlook comment should lean positive for Q4 and 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII has decided DNB's bigger results-day moves. Q1'26 NII and fees trailed consensus while PBT beat (https://www.placera.se/telegram/alphavalue-baader-europe-raises-forecasts-for-dnb-post-q1-earnings-20260507); Q2'26 PBT beat by about 2.7% and the stock moved -0.84%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside what the company guided, and the consensus was gathered after the 24 Sept hike. What may still be unpriced is the forward commentary on the 29 Nov repricing. The consensus has 2027 NII +4.2% over 2026 (64,498 vs 61,923), so an outlook above that is the only open part.
findings.independence: Q2 presentation NII bridge (spreads -511, repricing effective 12 July): https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/attachment?messageId=678131&attachmentId=329642; the 28 Sept rate release: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=683149

findings.finding: DNB said on 6 Oct that it is cutting about 400 FTEs in Technology & Services (about 4% of ~10,600 FTEs), with the restructuring cost booked in Q4 2026, the full cost effect from Q2 2027, and 'further information about the financial effects ... disclosed later this year'. The Q3 release is the natural place to quantify the charge and the run-rate saving, which is likely a few hundred million NOK a year and positive for 2027 cost estimates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior DNB release has quantified cost savings on results day. The stock rose +0.7% on the 6 Oct announcement (308.7 to 310.9) and gave it back over the following days.
findings.why_not_priced: The headcount is public and the money is not. The consensus cost line (-35,844m for 2026, -36,698m for 2027) cannot carry a saving the company has not sized. If it were priced, the consensus 2027 cost growth would be visibly below the 2026 run-rate plus wage inflation of 4.1-4.6% (it is +2.4%, so some saving may already sit in some estimates). That partial pricing is why this is small.
findings.independence: Norwegian version of the same release (683619), so not independent. Nothing else found.

findings.finding: On CET1 arithmetic a full 1.0% buyback at Q3 is less certain than the pattern suggests. Q2 CET1 was 17.4% after deducting the July programme's ~40bp, 100bp above the FSA's 16.4% expectation. The consensus Q3 CET1 is 17.49%, so another 1.0% would take headroom to roughly 70-80bp unless they lean on the +20bp Luminor completion effect, which comes later. A 0.5% programme (as at Q4'25) or a deferral is a real downside case on the line that has accompanied 3 of the last 4 releases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 1.0% announced with Q3'25 and the stock fell -4.98%; 0.5% with Q4'25 and +3.32%; 1.0% with Q2'26 and -0.84%. The buyback size alone has not set the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus 2026 'buybacks executed' spans NOK 3.8-17.7bn (average 10.6bn), so the street does not agree on the programme size, and the average implicitly prices roughly a repeat. A smaller programme would come as a surprise to about half of them. This is my inference from the CET1 numbers, not a company statement, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Q2 presentation: 'CET1 capital ratio of 17.4 per cent - 100 basis-point headroom to Financial Supervisory Authority's current expectation' (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/attachment?messageId=678131&attachmentId=329642). Peer sentiment on buybacks is fragile: Nordea paused its buyback on 15 Oct, 'pausar återköpen av egna aktier till dess att konsekvenserna för riskexponeringsbeloppet har förtydligats' (pauses share buybacks until the consequences for the risk exposure amount have been clarified), but that is an ECB model issue specific to Nordea (https://placera.se/nyheter/nordeas-rorelseresultat-som-vantat-pausar-aterkop-2026-10-15).

findings.finding: Consensus impairments of -706m already sit above the run-rate (Q2 -338m, Q1 -644m). The pre-close kept the asset-quality message unchanged while saying 'it would be natural to see more company-specific events', and Nordea's Q3 losses were 7bp, below its ~10bp norm, from 'a small number of corporate customers'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 impairments of -338 (corporate stage-3 events) came in a quarter where the stock moved -0.84%. Impairment surprises at DNB have been hundreds of millions NOK, about 2-5% of PBT.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is conservative relative to the run-rate, which is visible in the consensus file itself (low -1,656, high -408). A clean quarter is a few hundred million NOK upside that the average does not hold. It is a proxy for an unknowable number, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Nordea Q3 2026 net loan losses of EUR 74m (7bp), 'well within long term expectation of around 10bp': https://www.nordea.com/en/press/2026-10-15/third-quarter-results-2026

findings.finding: The pre-released Q3 one-offs, net gains of -383m (AT1 -534m, basis swaps +151m) and the ~NOK 1bn Luminor held-for-sale loss on the equity-method line, are in the 13 Oct consensus (other operating income average 565 against Q2's 1,664 for the same lines) and land exactly where the company said.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: These pre-releases come every quarter (Q1'26, Q2'26, Q4'25, Q3'25) and the results-day reaction has never been attributed to them.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Filed at 0 to record that the period's large non-operating items are already out.
